title: Splitting a finite etale marking into disjoint sections after alteration
statement: Let $g:X\to B$ be a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] morphism of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] between integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring] Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] schemes, whose generic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] over the generic point [def-sc-generic-point] $\eta$ of $B$ is a geometrically integral [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] curve [def-pc-curve]. Let $V\subseteq X$ be the open set of points at which $g$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $D\subset X$ be an effective Cartier divisor (a closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] locally cut out by one non-zero-divisor), possibly empty, with $D\subseteq V$ and $D\to B$ proper and etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Then there are an integral excellent Noetherian scheme $B_1$ and a finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] surjective morphism $b:B_1\to B$ with the following properties, where $X_1=X\times_BB_1$ [def-pc-fibre-product], $a:X_1\to X$ and $g_1:X_1\to B_1$ are the two projections, and $D_1=D\times_XX_1$. (i) $X_1$ is integral, excellent and Noetherian, and $a$ is finite and surjective. (ii) $g_1$ is proper, flat and of finite presentation; its generic fibre is a geometrically integral curve; for every geometric point $\bar t\to B_1$ the geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] of $g_1$ at $\bar t$ is isomorphic to the geometric fibre of $g$ at $b\circ\bar t$; and $g_1$ is smooth at every point of $a^{-1}(V)$. (iii) There are an integer $n\geq0$ and sections $s_1,\dots,s_n$ of $g_1$ (morphisms with $g_1s_i=1_{B_1}$), with pairwise disjoint images, such that $D_1$ is the disjoint union of the closed subschemes $s_1(B_1),\dots,s_n(B_1)$; in particular every $s_i$ lands in $a^{-1}(V)$, and $n=0$ when $D=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 0BQL (lemma-finite-etale-covering-normal-unramified), applied over the normalization of $B$ in a finite Galois extension of $\kappa(\eta)$ containing the residue fields of $D_\eta$; cf. literature/illusie-laszlo-orgogozo-travaux-de-gabber_arXiv-1207.3648.pdf, Exposé IX 1.4, p. 133 (normalized component of a base change). Integrality of $X_1$: flat base change of a geometrically integral generic fibre.

proof.text: The fibres of $D\to B$ are discrete unions of spectra of finite separable residue-field extensions by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points]. They are quasi-compact: base change preserves properness [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b), and a proper scheme over a field is of finite type, hence quasi-compact [def-weil-proper-morphism]. A quasi-compact discrete space is finite, since its singleton open cover has a finite subcover [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. The base $B$ is locally Noetherian, so [thm-pqf-finite-iff-proper-finite-fibres] makes $D\to B$ finite. In particular $D_\eta=\operatorname{Spec}C$ for a finite-dimensional commutative $K$-algebra $C$, where $K=\kappa(\eta)$.

source.place: Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field); Tag 01W4; Tag 02OG in coherent.tex, proper with finite fibres

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-generic-separable-algebra-splitting] to $C$: choose a finite separable extension $L/K$ such that $(C\otimes_K L)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a finite product of purely inseparable field extensions of $L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits](1) and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points], $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_K L)$ is a finite disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions of $L$. Thus $C\otimes_K L$ is already reduced, and each of its field factors is both separable and purely inseparable over $L$. Such a factor equals $L$: in positive characteristic a purely inseparable element has a power $p^r$ in $L$, so its minimal polynomial has only one distinct root, whereas a separable minimal polynomial has no repeated roots; consequently that polynomial has degree one. In characteristic zero pure inseparability already means equality [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. We have $D_\eta\times_K L\cong\coprod_{i=1}^n\operatorname{Spec}L$, for some $n\geq0$. If $D$ is empty, take $L=K$ and $n=0$.

source.place: Tags 02GO and 02GL (etale base change and etale schemes over fields); finite-algebra splitting as in the cited DAG lemma

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], $B$ is quasi-separated. Let $b:B_1\to B$ be the normalization of $B$ in $L$ [def-fin-normalization-extension]. The normalization theorem [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-in-residue-field-extension], applied at the generic point of the integral scheme $B$, says that $B_1$ is normal and integral and has function field $L$ compatibly over $B$. Since $B$ is covered by affine opens with excellent rings, every affine open of $B$ has an excellent ring by [lem-trf-excellent-scheme-affine-cover]. On an affine $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset B$, its inverse image is the spectrum of the integral closure of $R$ in $L$. The excellent domain $R$ is quasi-excellent, hence Nagata by [lem-exc-quasi-excellent-nagata], and N-2 by [lem-weil-pbc-nagata-domain-n2]. The definition [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain](2) makes that integral closure finite over $R$. Thus $b$ is finite. It is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](c), taking the target's identity as the proper map, and hence closed [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Its image contains the generic point of $B$, so closedness and integrality of $B$ give surjectivity.

source.place: Tags 035H, 035I, 035L (normalization); algebra.tex Tags 032F, 0334; more-algebra.tex Tag 07QV; properties.tex Tag 01OY

proof.text: Form $X_1=X\times_B B_1$ with projections $a,g_1$. Base change of the finite surjection $b$ makes $a$ finite and surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a) and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Both $B_1$ and $X_1$ are excellent and Noetherian: every affine open of $B$ and of $X$ has an excellent ring by [lem-trf-excellent-scheme-affine-cover], and these affine inverse images cover $B_1$ and $X_1$; on affine inverse images for the finite maps $b$ and $a$, their coordinate rings are finite algebras over excellent rings, hence finite type (module generators also generate the algebra) and excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]. Finite morphisms are of finite type by the same module-generator observation, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] gives Noetherianness of both schemes from that of $B$ and $X$.

The projection $g_1$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b), flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], and of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). The restriction $g|_V$ is smooth by the definition of the smooth locus. Its base change is $g_1|_{a^{-1}(V)}$, which is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). Thus every point of $a^{-1}(V)$ is a smooth point of $g_1$.

The generic point $\eta_1$ of $B_1$ has residue field $L$ and maps to $\eta$. Associativity of the defining fibre products gives $(X_1)_{\eta_1}\cong X_\eta\times_K L$. This is geometrically integral: for any field extension $E/L$ its base change is $X_\eta\times_K E$, integral by the original geometric-integrality hypothesis [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. It is proper over $L$, as the base change of the proper $g_1$ along $\operatorname{Spec}L\to B_1$ [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b), hence separated and of finite type over $L$ [def-weil-proper-morphism]; taking $E=L$ it is integral. It has dimension one by [lem-pc-dim-base-change], applied to the curve $X_\eta/K$ [def-pc-curve]. Thus it is a geometrically integral curve over $L$. For any geometric point $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to B_1$, the same fibre-product identity gives $X_1\times_{B_1}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\cong X\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, where the right-hand map to $B$ is $b\circ\bar t$. This compares geometric fibres over exactly the same algebraically closed field $\Omega$.

We verify integrality of the whole $X_1$, not just its generic fibre. Take a nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X_1$ mapping into an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq B_1$. The ring $R$ is a domain with fraction field $L$, since $B_1$ is integral with function field $L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], $A$ is flat over $R$. Tensoring the injection $R\hookrightarrow L$ with $A$ is injective by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], giving $A\hookrightarrow A\otimes_R L$. Since $U$ is nonempty, $A\neq0$, so the generic open $U_{\eta_1}=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R L)$ is nonempty. It is an affine open of the integral generic fibre from Step 6; hence $A\otimes_R L$, and therefore its subring $A$, is a domain. These opens $U$ cover $X_1$, so $X_1$ is reduced. Any two nonempty opens of $X_1$ contain such affine opens $U,U'$; their generic opens are nonempty opens of the same integral generic fibre, and therefore intersect. Hence any two nonempty opens of $X_1$ intersect, proving irreducibility. The generic fibre is nonempty, so $X_1$ is nonempty. Thus $X_1$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], completing (i).

source.place: Tag 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize); algebra.tex Tag 00HB (flat modules preserve injections); elementary affine integrality argument

proof.text: The two pullback descriptions identify $D_1=D\times_X X_1\cong D\times_B B_1$. It is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a), etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits](1), and a closed subscheme of $X_1$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). Put $T=\coprod_{i=1}^n B_1$, with structural map $q:T\to B_1$. The scheme coproduct exists with disjoint open-and-closed summands by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. The map $q$ is finite: over an affine $\operatorname{Spec}R$ its ring is $R^n$, generated as an $R$-module by the coordinate idempotents. It is etale, since on each summand it is the identity, so the affine-local etale definition holds there [def-weil-etale-morphism]. For $n=0$ the same descriptions use the zero algebra and the empty scheme. The generic fibre of $T$ is the disjoint union of $n$ copies of $\operatorname{Spec}L$, identified in Step 2 with that of $D_1$.

source.place: Tag 0BQL (finite etale covers over normal integral schemes); morphisms.tex Tags 01WL, 02GO, 01QR; schemes.tex Tags 01JB, 01JC

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-normal-integral-generic-hom-full] over the normal integral base $B_1$ to the finite etale covers $T,D_1$ of Step 8. The generic isomorphism $T_{\eta_1}\cong(D_1)_{\eta_1}$ and its inverse extend uniquely to $B_1$-morphisms $h:T\to D_1$ and $k:D_1\to T$. Their two composites restrict to the identity on the generic fibres. Uniqueness in the same cited statement, applied to each cover as both source and target, gives $kh=1_T$ and $hk=1_{D_1}$. Thus $h$ is an isomorphism over $B_1$. This uses full faithfulness on all finite etale covers, including empty and disconnected ones; it does not assume that $D_1$ is connected.

source.place: Tags 0BQL and 0BQM (proposition-normal, generic restriction is fully faithful)

proof.text: For each summand inclusion $\iota_i:B_1\to T$ set $s_i$ equal to $B_1\xrightarrow{\iota_i}T\xrightarrow{h}D_1\hookrightarrow X_1$. Since $h$ is over $B_1$, $g_1s_i=1_{B_1}$. The summands of $T$ are pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Their images under $h$ give a scheme-theoretic disjoint-union decomposition of $D_1$, and each is closed in $X_1$: compose its closed immersion into $D_1$ with $D_1\hookrightarrow X_1$ (locally the composite of the two quotient maps on rings is surjective). Thus these closed subschemes are exactly $s_i(B_1)$. Since $D\subseteq V$, the map $D_1\to X_1$ factors through $a^{-1}(V)$ by the defining pullback, so every section lands there. When $D=\varnothing$, Step 2 chose $n=0$ and this decomposition is empty. This proves (iii), while Steps 5 and 6 prove (ii).

The route works: excellence makes the normalization B_1 of B in L finite; D_1 is finite etale over B_1 and split on the generic fibre, so it is split over the normal integral base B_1. Total-space integrality of X_1 is proved correctly from flatness. No duplicate (the etale-local splitting nodes are different statements) and no cycle.
